This is a pretty good puzzle game.

Gameplay-wise, you're researching languages and cultural aspects of different peoples (tower inhabitants). The words are mostly resembled by a single character, and there's only written language in the game. If someone is talking to you verbally - you'll see the characters (and the voice will say some gibberish), so the game is simple, yet effective in this aspect.

The tower itself feels like a reference to the Babylon tower (language barrier problems). You won't really get lost in the words yourself though. The game features a verification mechanic for the words you learn. So once you're able to verify a certain group of words (and successfully manage to do it) - the game will handle those words itself from now on (putting it into appropriate forms and stuff).

The gameplay also contains some simpler puzzles and challenges, of course! If you feel like you're stuck on a puzzle - go look around for possible hints or necessary items. The game work well with those.

Achievement-wise - I managed to 100% the whole game in a single run. So if you're a completionist - just play the game as you would by yourself. There will be a certain point where the game will tell you not to progress until you finished certain things - go, finish those things, then collect all but the last 2 achievements, and finally go beat the game :)

언어를 해독하는 어드벤처 추리 게임입니다. 

플탐 
8시간 30분 걸렸습니다. 늦어도 10시간 안에는 끝날 것 같습니다.

장점
증거와 정답이 1대1로 매칭 되지 않기 때문에 여러 군데를 다니며 여러 간접 증거들을 모아야 합니다. 다소 부정확한 가설을 세워야 할 때도 있고 따라서 그 가설이 틀려서 한참 돌아가는 일도 많지만, 생각보다 불쾌한 경험은 아닙니다. "언어 해독" 이라는 탁월한 소재 선정 덕에 어드벤처 추리물로서의 단점들이 가려지는 듯 합니다.

스토리랄 건 크게 없고 단순하고 뻔한 플롯이지만 추리 소재에 잘 호응되고 신경쓰이는 정도는 아닙니다.

그래픽이나 사운드는 괜찮습니다.

단점
여러 대화를 보면서 추리를 하고 싶은데, 한번 본 대화를 모아서 볼 수 있는 기능이 없어서 일일이 대화가 일어났던 장소를 찾아 가야 합니다. 그러면서도 길 찾기가 필요 이상으로 복잡한데, 억지 플탐 늘리기라는 생각이 들 정도 입니다. 특히 극 후반부 1시간 정도는 추리 게임으로서의 정체성을 집어던지는 최악의 부분이었습니다. 

여러 언어가 등장하지만 언어별로 의미 추정 과정이 큰 차이가 없습니다. 현실에 존재하는 언어들 보다 문법이나 기호의 다양성이 떨어지는 것 같습니다. 

난이도 커브도 아쉽습니다. 각 언어의 입문 부분에서나 재밌고 아주 기본적인 문법을 익히면 확 쉬워지고 단순 노동이라 느껴집니다. 

총평
참신한 게임임에는 틀림 없지만 단점이 너무 많은 게임입니다. 추천하지 않습니다.

[h2]Spoilers ahead![/h2] This is a very personal review!!!
[b]If you haven’t finished the game yet, please don’t read this review![/b]


[i]“What if we could understand each other again?”[/i]
In the end, everything is connected.
No civilization can truly survive in complete isolation.

[hr][/hr]

[h2][Pros][/h2]

[h3]1. The overall visual design is absolutely beautiful.[/h3]

* I loved how each civilization had its own distinct color palette and unique language design.

[h3]2. The map feels confusing at first, but eventually realizing that every area is interconnected gives the world so much depth.[/h3]

* Discovering hidden paths and shortcuts was really fun too!
* It also reinforces the game’s central theme that, in the end, everyone is “connected” lol.

[h3]3. As you climb higher, the atmosphere gradually shifts from ancient to modern, which was fascinating.[/h3]

* Especially on the Anchorite floor (the top level), the cybernetic elements contrast so strongly with the earlier areas that it becomes visually striking.

[h3]4. The simple controls and straightforward dialogue balance nicely with the more complex puzzles and map design.[/h3]

* It all comes together surprisingly well during gameplay.

[h3]5. (A small thing, but) the upbeat music that plays after solving puzzles, or when climbing back to the top after finishing the ending, creates this oddly satisfying and exciting feeling haha.[/h3]

[h3]6. I loved how the credits show a full shot of the tower.[/h3]

* After spending the whole game trapped in these winding, circular interiors, finally seeing the tower from the outside just hits differently… you know what I mean.

[h3]7. I thought the game was basically over after finishing the main mechanic (deciphering the languages), but then suddenly every area became an “isolated zone” and the monster started chasing you…[/h3]

* It felt like the game continued reinforcing its themes and immersion right up until the very end.

But what exactly [i]is[/i] the monster?

* It seems to interfere with the connection between the tower’s civilizations.
* It brings death…
* And it always appears in places where communication has broken down.

Maybe it symbolizes the fear people fall into when they become isolated and unable to understand one another.
The terror that emerges when communication collapses.

* Also… what exactly was the alchemist’s “fairy” supposed to be?
  ...

[hr][/hr]

[h2][Cons][/h2]

[h3]1. The early game is REALLY rough.[/h3]

* The map is already complicated, and on top of that you’re trying to decipher languages while still figuring out how the game works… it gets exhausting fastㅠㅠ
* It takes a lot of patience before things finally “click.”
* Honestly, the beginning felt more stressful than fun for me.

* 2. ...............(And I have an absolutely terrible sense of direction.)............

[hr][/hr]

[h2][Characteristics of Each Civilization][/h2]

[h3]Floor 1 — The Abbey : Priests & Devotees [i]*Religion*[/i][/h3]

* The devotees keep searching for the priest… but I already saw the priest’s corpse…
* “God does not die.”
* They’re in conflict with the Warriors. (The Warriors shut the Abbey gates.)
* The people look toward the devotees / the devotees look toward God / the preacher speaks to the people / and God looks toward the instrument.
* Oh! The first-floor civilization constantly had visual motifs related to stars, but as you climb higher, the civilizations become increasingly isolated and withdrawn!!!! Right, that’s true~

[h3]Floor 2 — The Fortress : Warriors [i]*Power*[/i][/h3]

* “Warriors bear duty.” / “Warriors push back the impure.” / “The Chosen play instruments”… I think?
* To the Warriors:

  * “Impure” = the devotees
  * “Chosen” = the bards on the third floor lol
* “Warriors do not love death.”
* “But death loves warriors.”
* This area had a lot of imagery involving ships and bells.

[h3]Floor 3 — The Gardens : Bards [i]*Art*[/i][/h3]

* “We found freedom. Climbing higher is foolish.”

* “You fool lol”
  → and somehow [i]I[/i] ended up becoming the “Fool Bard”ㅠㅠㅋㅋㅋㅋㅋ

* They were kind of annoying, but once I reached the Alchemist floor they suddenly started talking about their “brothers.”

  * “The warriors are not our brothers.”

* They seem to have a friendly relationship with the alchemists.

[h3]Floor 4 — The Alchemists : [i]*Science*[/i][/h3]

* It seemed like they were experimenting with transformations and formulas in order to open the door sealed by the “fairies.”
* Gold, silver, copper, and carbon were the main materials.
* But it seems like the copper mine got shut down because of the monsterㅠㅠ

[h3]Floor 5 — The Top of the Tower : Anchorites [i]*Digital*[/i][/h3]

* “We have lost speech.”
* Apathy. Indifference. Pretending not to notice.
* After being disconnected for so long, they’ve completely abandoned language itself.
* Is this supposed to reflect our current reality?
* The way each civilization evolves from the past toward the present as you ascend the tower was really interesting haha.

画风美丽，配乐好听，故事设定也很有意思，逐步爬升将巴别塔的一切解开的过程体验感很好。除了部分潜行和追逐关卡之外整体上节奏是比较舒缓的，适合平静的时候慢慢玩。地图设计对路痴很不友好，迷路迷到我呕吐，至少花费了5个小时在找路上......文字破译的部分难度不算高，设计也比较有趣味性，但依然推荐自己准备一个笔记本来帮助破译。[spoiler] 各民族有各自的语法这个设计非常有意思（联通各层的时候差点被难死）， [/spoiler]结局做了一个非常有意思的设计，很震撼。地图引导和部分文字可能稍有瑕疵，但整体上仍然是一个很具有美感和趣味性的游戏，推荐游玩。

Nothing will ever quite compare to playing Outer Wilds for the first time (Which if you haven't played it, DON'T LOOK IT UP JUST PLAY IT BLIND), however this scratches the itch of solving puzzles and piecing together a story from clues. It is an amazing stand alone game, however my review is centered around its comparison to Outer Wilds since I found it in my search for games similar to it.
